company: San Roque Power Corporation (Marubeni 42.45%, Kansai Electric 7.5%, Sithe Energies 50.05%)
card_says: The company name on the card gives the shareholdings as Marubeni 42.45%, Kansai Electric 7.5% and Sithe Energies 50.05%.
source_says: By July 2006 the company was 92.5% owned by Marubeni, which had bought a 51% stake from Sithe Energies Inc, with the remaining 7.5% held by Kansai Electric. The split on the card may be the holding at the time of the loan; the 2006 report does not mention Sithe as a shareholder.

source.title: Marubeni completes power line from San Roque to Luzon grid

company: SEMOS (Société d'Exploitation des Mines d'Or de Sadiola)
card_says: Mine owner and operator, headquarters Bamako, Mali.
source_says: SEMOS was 41% AngloGold Ashanti, 41% Iamgold and 18% government of Mali at the time; both miners then sold their interests to Allied Gold Corporation and the government's stake rose to 20%, the sale completing on 31 December under an agreement announced in December 2019.

source.title: AngloGold, Iamgold complete Sadiola share sale

company: Roan Antelope Mining Corporation of Zambia (RAMCOZ)
card_says: Bought the Luanshya mines in 1997; owned by a group based in India; went bankrupt in late (year as given on the card).
source_says: The company is named 'Roan Antelope Copper Mines Limited (RAMCOZ)'; the Binani Group of Companies bought it in 1997 for US$35 million, and the Zambia National Commercial Bank put it under receivership rather than bankruptcy (the article gives 1997 in one passage and 2000 in another). The Luanshya mines passed to Luanshya Copper Mines in 2004 and liquidation had not begun as of the article.

source.title: A brief history of the privatization of mines in Zambia and RAMCOZ in particular

card_says: Majority owner of Interagua from mid-2008 (CAO); headquarters Madrid, Spain.
source_says: Proactiva was a 50:50 joint venture of Veolia Environnement and FCC; FCC sold its half to Veolia in June 2013 for 150 million euros, so Veolia has been the sole owner since then. The release describes Proactiva as a Latin American environmental services business and does not give a headquarters city.

source.title: FCC sells Veolia Environnement its 50% of Proactiva for 150 million euros

card_says: Held 43% through Malana Power; headquarters Oslo, Norway.
source_says: SN Power was wholly owned by Norfund, the Norwegian state investment fund, until Norfund agreed in October 2020 to sell it to Scatec for an equity value of US$1,166 million, with completion expected in the first half of 2021.

source.title: Scatec Solar acquires SN Power, building a global leader in renewable energy

card_says: Sponsor with a MIGA equity guarantee; headquarters Toronto, Canada.
source_says: Billiton Plc bought 95% of Rio Algom's shares on 6 October 2000 and the remainder in November 2000; by the year to 30 June 2002 it was an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of BHP Billiton Plc.

source.title: Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2002, Rio Algom Limited

card_says: Owner of the White River panel board factory.
source_says: Sonae Novobord was described in 2006 as part of Sonae Indústria. Since 2016 Sonae Indústria's wood-panel operations in Europe and South Africa, including the White River factory, have been held by Sonae Arauco, an equally owned joint venture of Sonae Indústria and Arauco; the Sonae Arauco milestones page records an upgrade of the White River factory in 2019 and does not say whether the Novobord company was renamed.

source.title: Milestones

company: Plantations et Huileries du Congo SA (PHC), subsidiary of Feronia Inc.
card_says: Operator of three plantations over more than 100,000 hectares; Feronia was listed in Toronto.
source_says: Feronia faced bankruptcy and was financially restructured from July 2020; in February 2022 the development finance institutions sold their debt to an affiliate of PHC's principal shareholder, KKM. PHC leases about 107,000 hectares, of which about 20,000 hectares are planted, and had 6,462 employees in November 2021.

source.title: PHC/Feronia overview

card_says: Australian company granted the railway concession in 2008.
source_says: Toll's board accepted a takeover offer from Japan Post in February 2015 and the company became a division of Japan Post on 28 May 2015, keeping its Melbourne head office and the Toll brand.

source.title: Our history

card_says: Seoul-based builder and 26 percent owner of the project company PNPC; headquarters Seoul, South Korea.
source_says: GlobalData's profile, filed under the name SK Engineering & Construction Co Ltd, describes the company as SK Ecoplant, a subsidiary of SK Inc based in Seoul. The page does not say when the name changed.

source.title: SK Ecoplant Co Ltd company profile

card_says: Holder and developer of Simandou blocks 3 and 4; headquarters London, United Kingdom.
source_says: SimFer, which holds the concession over blocks 3 and 4, is owned 85% by SimFer Jersey Limited and 15% by the Guinean state; SimFer Jersey is 53% Rio Tinto Group and 47% CIOH. Rio Tinto's holding is therefore indirect and partial.

source.title: Simandou iron-ore project, Guinea

company: SONACOS (Société nationale de commercialisation des oléagineux du Sénégal)
card_says: State oil-mill company; funded the private operators who replaced SONAGRAINES; slated for (privatisation, as given on the card).
source_says: SONACOS was privatised in 2005, bought by the French group Advens, and renamed SUNEOR SA in early 2007.

source.title: Suneor SA (African Growing Enterprises File)

card_says: State mining company whose payments to the central bank were attached.
source_says: ZCCM was formed in 1982; its main mine packages were sold to Anglo American by the end of March 2000 and ZCCM Investments Holdings was incorporated in 2000 to hold the state's remaining minority interests. In August 2015 the government transferred its 60.3% holding in ZCCM-IH to the Industrial Development Corporation Limited.

source.title: Timeline

card_says: Spanish company; bought the whole distribution system for US$115 million.
source_says: Gas Natural completed its purchase of Unión Fenosa in April 2009 and the combined company was named Gas Natural Fenosa, so Unión Fenosa no longer exists as a separate company.

source.title: De Catalana para el Alumbrado a Naturgy: 175 años y seis nombres para Gas Natural

card_says: Built the plant; a Marcos associate was charged with taking US$17 million from it; headquarters Pittsburgh, United States.
source_says: Westinghouse Electric Corporation renamed itself CBS Corporation in 1997 after selling its transmission and distribution business to ABB in 1989 and its defence and electronics business to Northrop Grumman in 1996; the nuclear power business was sold to British Nuclear Fuels Limited in 1998 and on to Toshiba in 2006.

card_says: Named by EJAtlas as the landfill operator, linked to the same group as Zoomlion.
source_says: The Fourth Estate names a 'Waste Landfills Company Limited' that received funds in 2022 to look after landfill sites across Ghana, in a passage about Jospong subsidiaries, but does not state who owns it. The Infra Global page on the Kpone landfill names only Zoomlion Ghana Limited, contracted to decommission the site, finished in 2013 under UESP2, with a further 18-month contract from 1 June 2020.
